question: Does a larger variance always mean a worse dataset or model?
direct_answer: No. It just means the values are more spread out.
expanded_answer: Variance is not inherently good or bad. Sometimes high spread is expected and meaningful, while in other cases it may indicate instability or noise. The interpretation depends on the task and the feature.
key_points: High variance can be useful or problematic
common_wrong_ideas: Large variance is always an error
